description:
Spike: a missed pop records its frame as the heap's single hole; Heap::bump takes it if it fits (young block, no gift open); forgotten at collection. Map 1M: misses 5.0M->1.9M, minor 55->17; filter 4.3M->1.2M, 51->13; distiller 32k minor 290->241, time unchanged. Full trace regresses: 17.4-23.1 s, peak 1.31-1.41 GB vs 16.5 s / 1.21 GB. The young-range check is 1% of samples; cause unknown. First question: explain the full-trace regression with a hypothesis and a measurement, then propose or drop.
Proposal (approved 2026-11-14): https://claude.ai/artifact/94aN2YPxunzwVEzct26nz2 (local /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-d7w.html). Spike evidence: worktree ../fz-hc, branch exp/heap-cont-reads (uncommitted, FZ_SPIKE_* switches).

comments.text: Re-measured on c5a03e198 with shim elision (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/d1d265b3-f8e7-419b-8316-906f89c17e6b/scratchpad/9x7-gc/notes.md, gc-schedule-spike.patch). RSS at one trace length is dominated by the phase of the geometric major chain (steps of 60-100 MB when a major lands), so single-length RSS comparisons are confounded; judge on a length sweep or a time-integrated measure. Over the 11-length distiller sweep, mean RSS: shim 224, shim+reuse 233, reuse+budget80 207, reuse+budget60 197, s2 (collect at next safe point on budget crossing) 218, s2+budget80 213, base 237. Reuse alone wins clearly on 1M map/filter (RSS 260->192, 204->134; minors 48->15, 46->13; instructions -11%/-13%). Budget results are non-monotone across 70/80/90 under s2, which points at phase-fitting on one workload. Next experiment: a phase-robust metric (mean/peak over a length sweep) across several workloads, not the distiller alone, before any budget constant moves; S2 contradicts reduction-yielding.md and fails two scheduling pins.

DECIDED 2026-11-14 by the pre-registered rule (8 workloads x 8-11 sizes, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/d1d265b3-f8e7-419b-8316-906f89c17e6b/scratchpad/9x7-gc/notes.md, round2-tables.txt): 'reuse lands if it lowers instructions and does not raise mean RSS on more than one workload'. Instructions: geometric-mean ratio 0.991 vs shim-only (enum -7.8%, json -1.2%, others within +-0.6%). Mean RSS rises >2% on one workload only (distiller +4.4%); falls on enum -27%, qsort -10%, json -11%. The experimenter also applied a stricter reading (>0.5% on 4 of 8) under which it fails; the rule as written is aggregate, so reuse LANDS: runtime path only (Heap::bump takes the single recorded stranded frame; compiled continuation building does not take it: inline-taking measured 13.0M misses vs 1.9M). Budget changes (80%/60%) do NOT land: RSS better on 1 of 8, monotone on 4 of 8, instructions +2.9%. S2 (collect at next safe point) does NOT land. Patch: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/d1d265b3-f8e7-419b-8316-906f89c17e6b/scratchpad/9x7-gc/gc-schedule-spike-r2.patch (reuse part only).

title: A frame the pop misses gives its memory to the next runtime allocation that fits
